CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Stay at the table and convert the 19 May joint statement into a narrow, executable purchase package (agriculture and energy we can actually absorb) sufficient to keep Section 301 tariffs off and to close a ZTE settlement. Do not put a $200 billion number on paper, do not offer structural rollback of industrial policy or JV/licensing rules, and do not fire the unused $50 billion retaliatory list while Mnuchin has the tariff war on hold. Use the forthcoming Ross visit to lock in those two deliverables and keep Lighthizer's unused legal tools from being triggered.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not high. The 16 April ZTE denial order demonstrated that a US export-control stroke can shut a national telecom champion (70k+ jobs, major operations halted), which is the firm-level tech-coercion channel in the +0.5 CHN anchor. The 3 April Section 301 list still aims at aerospace, ICT, robotics and machinery — Made in China 2025 sectors — and Lighthizer said after the joint statement that forced tech transfer, cyber theft and innovation remain unresolved and that tariffs, investment restrictions and export regulations remain available. Those two facts keep threat above zero. It is not +0.5 because the $50 billion 301 duties are not in force (hearings 15–17 May; post-hearing comments only just closed), Mnuchin has publicly put the trade war on hold, Trump on 13 May instructed Commerce to get ZTE back in business, China's industrial production is still ~6.8% y/y, merchandise exports are still growing, reserves are ~$3.13 trillion with only a ~1% drift, and CNY has strengthened versus the dollar over the window rather than coming under FX pressure. Action should therefore be mild and slightly de-escalatory, not a further tariff volley and not a structural concession. Escalating now would likely collapse the ceasefire, invite the 301 list onto MIC 2025 goods, and leave ZTE dead. Full or large purchase/structural concession would pay for a pause the US has already offered and would trade away industrial-policy core for a statement CSIS's Kennedy correctly called too vague to bind. Negotiate: specify enough ag/energy purchases to satisfy the US political need to show deficit reduction, extract a written ZTE path and a continued 301 stay, and keep IP/industrial-policy talks in a long channel rather than a one-shot giveaway.
key_factors: Section 301 $50B list proposed and through hearings but not implemented; Mnuchin says tariffs are on hold
ZTE 7-year denial order still legally in force after operational shutdown, but Trump publicly directed Commerce to restore the firm
19 May joint statement commits China only to a vague significant increase in US goods/services, especially ag and energy, with a US team to follow
Lighthizer has reserved tariffs, investment restrictions and export controls on unresolved IP/tech-transfer issues
China real economy not yet bitten: IP ~6.8% y/y, exports still up, reserves ~$3.13T, CNY firmer vs USD
China already imposed the $3B 232 retaliation and tabled a $50B 301 counter-list; further escalation would blow the ceasefire
US matching offer is a tariff pause plus a ZTE political opening, not a structural IP settlement — so purchases can be discussed but industrial-policy rollback should not

sources_cited.excerpt: US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold." Markets rally.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.

USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
China industrial production still expanding: latest 106.8 (index, same period previous year=100) as of 2018-05-01.
China total reserves ex-gold ~$3.129 trillion as of 2018-05-01; only ~0.95% decline over the window — no reserve-stress signal.
CNY/USD 6.3875 on 2018-05-23 versus 6.5967 on 2017-11-27 — yuan stronger, not a depreciation/FX-pressure episode.
China merchandise exports still growing: latest $208.4bn SA in May 2018 vs $203.9bn in Dec 2017 (+2.2%).

Mnuchin: "We're putting the trade war on hold" and tariffs are on hold while executing the framework; Lighthizer: forced technology transfers, cyber theft and innovation remain far more important, and the US may still use tariffs, investment restrictions and export regulations.

Joint statement: China will significantly increase purchases of US goods and services; meaningful increases in agriculture and energy; US will send a team to work out details; China will advance Patent Law and other IP amendments. No dollar figure, no ZTE language, no tariff rollback language.

Statement silent on whether the US suspends the $50–150bn tariff plans or eases ZTE; public-comment deadline on the $50bn list ends the following week; China had been reported to offer ~$200bn in extra US exports but that language is not in the statement.

13 May: Trump tweets he and Xi are working to get ZTE back in business fast after the firm halted major operating activities under the Commerce denial order; White House says Ross will exercise independent judgment on the regulatory action.
